T0606.title: Humanoid Robot
T0606.definition: A robot with a human-like body structure (head, torso, two arms, two legs) that can perform human-like actions such as walking, grasping, and tool use; one of the main carrier forms of embodied intelligence.
T0606.description: Humanoid robots have rapidly developed in recent years, with representative products including Tesla Optimus, Figure 02, Unitree G1/H1, Agility Digit, and Boston Dynamics Atlas. Their human-like body design lets them adapt to human-designed environments (stairs, doors, tools), but also brings unique security risks: dynamic-stability constraints of bipedal walking, large kinetic energy, and physical-harm risk from close human collaboration. Figure AI established a humanoid-robot safety center; its former product-safety lead sued claiming the robot's force is enough to crush a human skull. Humanoid robots mostly use a teleoperation+autonomy hybrid mode; Tesla Optimus was disclosed as partly human-operated at the We, Robot event.
T0606.usageExample: When a humanoid robot collaborates with humans to carry parts in a factory, a bypassed e-stop or force-control failure may cause serious worker injury.
